introduction-the-digital-front-door.core: API Gateway is a managed front door for APIs: it terminates TLS, authenticates and authorises callers, throttles and meters usage, validates and transforms requests, routes to backends (Lambda, HTTP, AWS services, private VPC resources) and emits logs and metrics, so backends focus on business logic.

first_principles.problem: Every microservice re-implements auth, rate limiting and request validation inconsistently.
truths: A single entry point simplifies security.

analogy.title: A hotel reception desk
analogy.story: Checks ID, hands out keys, limits how many guests enter and directs them to the right room.
analogy.breaks: Reception desks have queues; API Gateway scales to thousands of requests per second automatically.

check.q: What cross-cutting concerns does API Gateway typically handle?
check.a: Authentication/authorisation, throttling, request validation, routing and logging.

rest-apis-vs-http-apis-the-decision-matr.core: HTTP APIs are cheaper (~70% less) and faster, with JWT authorizers, Lambda and HTTP integrations, CORS and private integrations: ideal for most proxies. REST APIs add API keys and usage plans, request validation and transformation (VTL), AWS WAF, caching, edge-optimised and private endpoints, and direct AWS service integrations.

first_principles.problem: A team picks REST APIs by default and pays more for features it never uses, or picks HTTP APIs and later needs WAF and usage plans.
derivation: **HTTP API** for simple, low-latency Lambda/HTTP proxies with JWT.
**REST API** for usage plans, API keys, caching, WAF, VTL transforms, private endpoints.

analogy.title: Economy versus business class
analogy.story: Both fly you there; business adds lounges and perks at a higher price.
analogy.breaks: Upgrading seats is easy; switching API types means rebuilding config.

example.title: Two APIs
flow: Internal mobile backend, JWT, Lambda → HTTP API
Public partner API with keys, quotas, WAF → REST API
example.outcome: right API type per use case.

check.q: Which API Gateway type supports usage plans and API keys?

endpoint-types-edge-regional-private.core: REST APIs have three endpoint types. Edge-optimised routes clients through CloudFront's edge (AWS-managed distribution) for geographically spread clients. Regional serves clients in the same region or behind your own CloudFront. Private is reachable only from VPCs through interface endpoints, with resource policies restricting access.

first_principles.problem: An internal API is publicly reachable, and a global API is slow for distant users.
truths: You may want to control your own CDN.
derivation: **Edge-optimised** for global clients without your own CDN.
**Regional** + your own CloudFront for control (caching, WAF at edge).
**Private** via execute-api VPC endpoint + resource policy.

analogy.title: A shop's entrances
analogy.story: A storefront on the high street (edge), a local entrance (regional) or a staff-only back door (private).
analogy.breaks: Shops have fixed doors; you can change endpoint type later with some reconfiguration.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Only callers via that VPC endpoint can invoke.

check.q: How is a private API Gateway endpoint reached?
check.a: Through an execute-api interface VPC endpoint, restricted by a resource policy.

throttling-the-token-bucket-algorithm.core: API Gateway throttles with token buckets: a steady rate (requests per second refill) and a burst (bucket size). Limits apply at account/region level, then stage and method level, and per client via usage plans with API keys. Excess requests get 429 Too Many Requests, and clients should retry with exponential backoff and jitter.

first_principles.problem: One client's retry storm consumes the account's limit and throttles everyone else.
truths: Bursts are normal; sustained overload isn't.

analogy.title: Tokens dripping into a cup at a turnstile
analogy.story: Each entry uses a token; a full cup allows a short rush, then entries match the drip rate.
analogy.breaks: Turnstiles block physically; clients can ignore 429s and keep retrying unless they're well-behaved.

example.title: Usage plan tiers
flow: Pro tier: 200 rps, burst 400, no quota

check.q: What status code does API Gateway return when throttling?

custom-authorizers-the-lambda-bouncer.core: A Lambda authorizer runs your code to validate a token (TOKEN type) or request parameters (REQUEST type) and returns an IAM policy (REST) or simple allow/deny with context (HTTP API). Results are cached by identity source for a TTL, so the authorizer doesn't run on every call. Use it for custom tokens, external IdPs or fine-grained rules.

first_principles.problem: An API must validate tokens from a legacy identity system that isn't OIDC-compatible.
truths: Not all identity systems issue JWTs.
Running auth per request adds latency and cost.
derivation: Set **cache TTL** with the right identity sources.

analogy.title: A nightclub bouncer with a custom guest list
analogy.story: Checks your ID against their rules and stamps your hand so you don't queue again for a while.
analogy.breaks: Hand stamps are checked by eye; cached policies must cover all routes the caller will use.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Backend receives trusted userId and tenant.

check.a: To avoid invoking the authorizer on every request, reducing latency and cost.

integration-types-how-api-gateway-connec.core: Integrations connect routes to backends: Lambda proxy (full request to Lambda), HTTP proxy (to any URL), AWS service integrations (directly call SQS, DynamoDB, Step Functions without Lambda), private integrations via VPC Link to NLB/ALB/Cloud Map, and mock integrations. Proxy integrations pass everything through; non-proxy ones transform with mapping templates.

first_principles.problem: A Lambda exists only to forward requests into SQS, adding cost and latency.
truths: Glue functions add latency and failure points.
API Gateway can call AWS APIs directly.
derivation: **AWS service integration** to skip glue Lambdas.

analogy.title: A receptionist routing calls
analogy.story: Some go to staff (Lambda), some to another office (HTTP), some straight into the post tray (SQS).
analogy.breaks: Receptionists can improvise; integrations need explicit mappings.

example.title: Direct SQS integration
flow: API Gateway SendMessage to SQS with IAM role

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: No glue Lambda; lower latency and cost.

check.q: How can API Gateway put a message on SQS without Lambda?
check.a: Using an AWS service integration that calls SQS SendMessage with an IAM role.
